mappings.name: a merchant's webhook receiver: accept anything POSTed

metadata.why:
This is a MERCHANT's receiver, not a rail stub: it stands in for the endpoint `merchant_clients[].webhooks[].url` names, reached over HTTP exactly as a real merchant's would be (ADR-0006 / AGENTS.md rule 1). It matches any path because the endpoint URL is configuration and a suite or a compose overlay may point at any of them, and any body because vpay decides what it signs — a mapping that matched a body shape would silently 404 the day the envelope changed, which is the one failure this receiver must not hide.

Priority 10, the low end, so the `/flaky` scenario mappings (priority 1) win on their own path. WireMock's lowest number wins.

The 200 is the whole contract: `vpay_worker::webhooks::handle_deliver` treats any 2xx as delivered and everything else as one more rung of the ladder. Requests are read back from `GET /__admin/requests`, which is where the signature-parity tests get the exact bytes and the `Vpay-Signature` header from.
